input: In the git repository /home/eval/reports, `make` builds build/report.txt from data/*.csv using the awk scripts in lib/ and data/regions.map. After recent commits the report is stale and `make` says there is nothing to do. Fix the Makefile so that build/report.txt is rebuilt whenever anything it is derived from changes, including when a new data/*.csv file is added; `make test` checks this with `make -q` on a scratch copy. Do not edit tests/, lib/ or data/. Then run plain `make` so build/report.txt is current, and commit the Makefile with a message starting with `build:`.

transcript.final_response:
I fixed the Makefile, and `make test` now passes. I ran plain `make` and `build/report.txt` is current. I committed only the Makefile, with the message `build: track all csv inputs, scripts and regions.map as dependencies`.

**What was wrong:** `SUMS` was hard-coded to `eu` and `us`, so `data/apac.csv` was never built into the report. The report rule also didn't list `lib/fmt.awk` or `data/regions.map` as dependencies. The `.sum` rule didn't list `lib/sum.awk`.

**What changed:**
- `SUMS` is now derived from `$(wildcard data/*.csv)`, so a new CSV is picked up automatically.
- `build/%.sum` depends on its CSV, `lib/sum.awk` and the Makefile.
- `build/report.txt` depends on all the sums, `lib/fmt.awk`, `data/regions.map` and the Makefile.
- The report command now uses `$(SUMS)` instead of `$^`, because `$^` would also include the new script and map prerequisites.

The rebuilt report now includes Australia, Canada and Japan from `apac.csv`.

**Left uncommitted:** `build/apac.sum` is a new generated file, and I left it untracked. The other `build/*` files were already tracked, so say if you want it committed as well. I also removed the scratch `build/deps-check` directory and `build/test-report.txt` that the test run created.

cd /home/eval/reports && cat tests/test_deps.sh; cat lib/*.awk; cat data/regions.map; cat .gitignore; git ls-files

cd /home/eval/reports && cat > Makefile <<'EOF'
CSVS := $(wildcard data/*.csv)
SUMS := $(patsubst data/%.csv,build/%.sum,$(CSVS))

all: build/report.txt

build/%.sum: data/%.csv lib/sum.awk Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	awk -F, -f lib/sum.awk $< | sort > $@

build/report.txt: $(SUMS) lib/fmt.awk data/regions.map Makefile
	awk -f lib/fmt.awk data/regions.map $(SUMS) | sort > $@

test:
	@bash tests/test_deps.sh

.PHONY: all test
EOF
make && make test; cat build/report.txt; git status --short

cd /home/eval/reports && rm -rf build/deps-check build/test-report.txt && make && git add Makefile && git commit -qm "build: track all csv inputs, scripts and regions.map as dependencies" && git status --short && git log --oneline | head -3

#!/bin/bash
# Checks the Makefile dependency graph with `make -q` on a scratch copy:
# touching any input must make build/report.txt out of date.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
t=build/deps-check
inputs="lib/sum.awk lib/fmt.awk data/regions.map data/eu.csv data/us.csv data/apac.csv"
rm -rf "$t"; mkdir -p "$t"
cp -R Makefile lib data "$t"/
make -s -C "$t" build/report.txt > /dev/null || { echo "FAIL: make build/report.txt"; exit 1; }
cmp -s tests/expected-report.txt "$t/build/report.txt" || { echo "FAIL: report differs from tests/expected-report.txt"; exit 1; }
reset() {
  (cd "$t" && touch -d '2001-01-01 00:00:00' Makefile $inputs \
    && touch -d '2002-01-01 00:00:00' build/*.sum \
    && touch -d '2002-01-01 00:00:01' build/report.txt)
}
reset
make -q -C "$t" build/report.txt || { echo "FAIL: fresh build is not up to date"; exit 1; }
fail=0
for f in $inputs; do
  reset
  touch -d '2003-01-01 00:00:00' "$t/$f"
  if make -q -C "$t" build/report.txt; then
    echo "FAIL: touching $f leaves build/report.txt up to date"; fail=1
  else
    echo "ok   $f"
  fi
done
reset
printf 'region,amount\nBR,7\n' > "$t/data/latam.csv"
if make -q -C "$t" build/report.txt; then echo "FAIL: new data/latam.csv not picked up"; fail=1; fi
make -s -C "$t" build/report.txt > /dev/null
grep -q '^BR ' "$t/build/report.txt" || { echo "FAIL: data/latam.csv missing from the report"; fail=1; }
if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then echo PASS | tee build/test-report.txt; else echo FAIL > build/test-report.txt; exit 1; fi
# fmt.awk: first file maps region codes to names; the rest are "code total" lines
FNR == NR { name[$1] = $2; next }
{ printf "%-14s %6d\n", ($1 in name ? name[$1] : $1), $2 }
# sum.awk: total the amount column per region code (header skipped)
NR > 1 { t[$1] += $2 }
END { for (k in t) print k, t[k] }
